subject: econ
source: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 syllabus 2027–2029, Cambridge International

weeks.topic: Economic development: living standards and the Human Development Index
objectives: Compare GDP per head and HDI as indicators
Evaluate measures of living standards

weeks.topic: Poverty: absolute and relative, causes and policies
objectives: Distinguish absolute and relative poverty
Evaluate policies to reduce poverty

weeks.topic: Population: growth, structure and population pyramids
objectives: Explain birth rates, death rates and migration
Interpret population pyramids

weeks.topic: Differences in economic development between countries
objectives: Explain causes of differences in development
Compare developed and developing economies

weeks.topic: International specialisation and free trade
objectives: Explain specialisation at national level
Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of free trade

weeks.topic: Globalisation and multinational companies
objectives: Define globalisation and its causes
Evaluate the impact of multinational companies on host countries

weeks.topic: Trade protection: tariffs, quotas, subsidies and embargoes
objectives: Describe methods of trade protection
Evaluate the reasons for and consequences of protection

weeks.topic: Foreign exchange rates: floating and fixed systems
objectives: Explain how floating exchange rates are determined
Identify causes of exchange rate fluctuations

weeks.topic: Consequences of exchange rate changes
objectives: Analyse effects of appreciation and depreciation on trade
Link exchange rates to inflation and growth

weeks.topic: The current account of the balance of payments
objectives: Identify the components of the current account
Calculate current account balances

weeks.topic: Current account deficits and surpluses: causes, consequences and policies
objectives: Explain causes of current account imbalances
Evaluate policies to correct a deficit

weeks.topic: Conflicts between macroeconomic aims
objectives: Explain trade-offs such as growth versus inflation
Analyse policy conflicts using examples

weeks.topic: Evaluating the effectiveness of government policies
objectives: Assess fiscal, monetary and supply-side policies
Consider time lags and side effects

weeks.topic: Economic data skills: tables, graphs and percentage changes
objectives: Interpret economic data accurately
Calculate percentage changes and index numbers

weeks.topic: Term 1 review: economic development and international trade
objectives: Consolidate development, trade and exchange rate topics
Practise structured questions

weeks.topic: Applied microeconomics: demand and supply diagrams in current events
objectives: Apply diagrams to news stories
Explain market changes clearly

weeks.topic: Applied macroeconomics: inflation, unemployment and growth in the news
objectives: Link news reports to macroeconomic concepts
Evaluate likely policy responses

weeks.topic: Case study: Brazil and other emerging economies
objectives: Analyse development challenges in emerging economies
Use Brazilian data to support arguments

weeks.topic: Case study: Brazil's trade, Mercosur and major trading partners
objectives: Analyse Brazil's export structure and partners
Evaluate the benefits of regional trade agreements

weeks.topic: Calculation skills: PED, PES, costs, inflation and exchange rates
objectives: Carry out common economic calculations
Interpret results in context

weeks.topic: Synoptic links between microeconomics and macroeconomics
objectives: Connect market analysis to macroeconomic outcomes
Build chains of reasoning across topics

weeks.topic: Paper 1 practice: multiple-choice techniques
objectives: Apply elimination strategies
Read diagrams and data quickly and accurately

weeks.topic: Paper 2 practice: the compulsory data response question
objectives: Extract and interpret information from source material
Answer with explicit reference to data

weeks.topic: Paper 2 practice: analysis with accurate diagrams
objectives: Draw fully labelled diagrams
Explain diagrams in written analysis

weeks.topic: Paper 2 practice: 'discuss' questions and balanced evaluation
objectives: Present arguments for and against
Reach a justified conclusion

weeks.topic: Exam technique: command words and structuring answers
objectives: Interpret command words such as define, explain, analyse and discuss
Allocate time according to marks

weeks.topic: Mock exams: Paper 1 and Paper 2
objectives: Sit both papers under exam conditions
Analyse results to plan revision

weeks.topic: Revision: the basic economic problem and allocation of resources
objectives: Revise PPCs, demand, supply and elasticity
Practise diagram-based questions

weeks.topic: Revision: microeconomic decision makers
objectives: Revise banks, households, workers and unions
Revise firms, costs and market structure

weeks.topic: Revision: government and the macroeconomy
objectives: Revise macroeconomic aims and policies
Practise growth, unemployment and inflation questions

weeks.topic: Revision: economic development
objectives: Revise living standards, poverty and population
Practise comparison questions

weeks.topic: Revision: international trade and globalisation
objectives: Revise trade, protection and exchange rates
Practise current account questions

weeks.topic: Revision: full past-paper practice
objectives: Complete timed past papers
Compare answers with mark schemes

weeks.topic: Final exams: Paper 1 Multiple Choice
objectives: Sit Paper 1 across the whole syllabus
Manage time and check answers

weeks.topic: Final exams: Paper 2 Structured Questions
objectives: Sit Paper 2 with data response and structured questions
Use diagrams and evaluation effectively

weeks.topic: Exam season: targeted practice between papers
objectives: Review errors from papers already taken
Keep definitions and diagrams fresh

objectives: Reflect on the IGCSE course
Preview IB Economics microeconomics and the role of evaluation
